setup: Set an adjustable bench to an incline of approximately 30 to 45 degrees.
Sit on the bench with a dumbbell resting upright on each knee.
Plant your feet firmly on the floor and retract your shoulder blades against the backrest.
Kick the dumbbells back with your knees one at a time as you lean back onto the bench, pressing them into a locked-out position over your upper chest.
steps: Lower the dumbbells under control toward your upper chest, allowing your elbows to track at roughly a 45-degree to 60-degree angle relative to your torso.
Descend until you achieve a comfortable stretch in the pectorals, keeping your forearms perpendicular to the floor.
Press the dumbbells up and slightly inward along a natural arc until your arms are extended, without banging the weights together at the top.
instructions.breathing: Inhale deeply during the lowering eccentric phase, and exhale powerfully as you press past the sticking point.
cues: Tuck elbows slightly toward the ribs, avoiding a flared 90-degree angle.
Keep the wrists stacked directly over the elbows.
Drive the floor away with your feet to keep the torso stable.

common_faults.fault: Setting the bench angle too steep (greater than 45 degrees).
common_faults.correction: Keep the bench at 30 to 45 degrees to maintain tension on the clavicular head of the chest rather than completely shifting load to the anterior deltoids.

common_faults.fault: Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
common_faults.correction: Tuck the elbows roughly 45 to 60 degrees to protect the shoulder joint and better align with upper pectoral muscle fibers.

common_faults.fault: Bouncing or colliding the dumbbells at the top.
common_faults.correction: Maintain tension throughout the movement by stopping just short of full lockout and keeping the dumbbells separated by a few inches.

precautions: If experiencing muscle failure, drop the dumbbells safely away from your body to the rubber flooring or guide them carefully back to your thighs while sitting up.

name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
summary: An upper-body compound pressing movement performed on an inclined bench to target the upper chest, anterior shoulders, and triceps.
